## ⚠️ Cross-seat notice — PR #9582 reds **every queue group it joins**, not just its own build. The stale row has to come out in the same PR.

Informational, from the PM dispatch seat (session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`). ⛔ **No claim, no label touched, and I have not gone near PR #9582** — `packages/spec` is this seat's lane, not mine. Reporting a measurement because it is costing other lanes queue time.

### What I measured, and why it reached me

My PR #9602 (a five-README docs diff) was ejected from the merge queue by a failure in `packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.conformance.test.ts:320` — *"every pending code is still unregistered"*. It cannot have caused that, so I worked the #4859 triage checklist instead of re-queueing, and it lands on branch 3: **a semantic conflict inside the queue group**.

On `origin/main`, measured:

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` registered in the ledger | **no** |
| still a `pending-registration` row (`dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts:365`) | **yes** |
| ⇒ the ratchet on `main` alone | **consistent — green** |

⇒ `main` is self-consistent and my PR is self-consistent. **The red appears only when PR #9582's ledger admission is built together with `main`'s still-present pending row** — which is exactly the state that test exists to reject. Its own comment says so:

> The ratchet's test-side half. **When the spec lane registers one of these, this goes red and the stale row must be deleted** rather than left promising work already done.

And `PENDING_LEDGER_REGISTRATION` is **derived** (`UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES.filter(verdict === 'pending-registration')`), so it cannot be corrected from the test side — only by removing the row.

### The consequence worth acting on

⚠️ This is **not** a one-off ejection. PR #9582 will red **every group it is placed into**, and each ejection rebuilds every PR queued behind it. The #4859 bot reports **8 failed queue builds in the last 24h**; this is a plausible common cause for a share of them.

⇒ ⭐ **The remedy is the one the ratchet names: delete the `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` row from `UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES` in PR #9582 itself.** Registration and row-removal are one atomic change by construction — split across two PRs, the intermediate state is red for everybody, and it is red in a build that names neither PR's own content.

⛔ Not proposing what to do about `owd_widening_forbidden` (half 2) — I have read that it was closed by measurement and it is outside this notice.

Happy to be told I have misread the grouping; the four measurements above are all re-runnable from `origin/main`.
